Disable face culling or enable back-face culling to render the front faces of the cube [S1, unofficial][S3, unofficial].

The claim states that one should 'Disable face culling or enable back-face culling to render the front faces of the cube'. Source [S1] explicitly describes a two-pass rendering technique. In Pass 2, it states: 'Render the cube geometry with back face culling enabled (`gl.cullFace(gl.BACK)`) and culling disabled (`gl.disable(gl.CULL_FACE)`) to the screen.' Enabling back-face culling (`gl.BACK`) causes the GPU to discard back-facing polygons, thereby rendering only the front-facing polygons. Disabling culling also results in rendering front faces (along with back faces, but the front faces are indeed rendered). Thus, both methods mentioned in the claim are supported by the evidence in Source [S1] as valid ways to render the front faces (specifically in the context of the second pass where front coordinates are needed).
